assertions.description: getPathData() on d="M0 0 l10 10" returns two {type, values} segments that keep the authored command letters ("M", then relative "l") and their numbers.
assertions.test: (() => { const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); p.setAttribute('d', 'M0 0 l10 10'); if (typeof p.getPathData !== 'function') return false; const r = p.getPathData(); return Array.isArray(r) && r.length === 2 && r[0].type === 'M' && r[1].type === 'l' && r[1].values.length === 2 && r[1].values[0] === 10 && r[1].values[1] === 10; })()

assertions.description: getPathData({normalize: true}) reduces relative, H/V, quadratic and arc segments to absolute M, L, C and Z only (relative h10 from 5,5 becomes L 15 5).
assertions.test: (() => { const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); p.setAttribute('d', 'M5 5 h10 v10 q5 5 10 0 a5 5 0 0 1 5 5 z'); if (typeof p.getPathData !== 'function') return false; const r = p.getPathData({ normalize: true }); return r.length >= 6 && r.every((s) => 'MLCZ'.includes(s.type) && s.type.length === 1) && r[1].type === 'L' && r[1].values[0] === 15 && r[1].values[1] === 5; })()

assertions.description: getPathData() on a path with no d attribute returns an empty array.
assertions.test: (() => { const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); if (typeof p.getPathData !== 'function') return false; const r = p.getPathData(); return Array.isArray(r) && r.length === 0; })()

assertions.description: setPathData() accepts plain {type, values} objects and the element's d attribute then reads back the same segments.
assertions.test: (() => { const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); if (typeof p.setPathData !== 'function' || typeof p.getPathData !== 'function') return false; p.setPathData([{ type: 'M', values: [1, 2] }, { type: 'C', values: [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] }, { type: 'Z', values: [] }]); const d = p.getAttribute('d'); const r = p.getPathData(); return !!d && r.length === 3 && r[1].type === 'C' && r[1].values[5] === 8 && r[2].type === 'Z'; })()

assertions.description: setPathData([{}]) throws a TypeError because type and values are required dictionary members (structural validation), rather than silently accepting the object.
assertions.test: (() => { const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); if (typeof p.setPathData !== 'function') return false; try { p.setPathData([{}]); return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: getPathData() returns the d attribute's base value even when the CSS d property renders a different shape.
assertions.test: (() => { const svg = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'svg'); const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); if (typeof p.getPathData !== 'function') return false; p.setAttribute('d', 'M0 0 L10 10'); p.style.setProperty('d', 'path("M0 0 L50 50 L90 0")'); svg.append(p); document.body.append(svg); const r = p.getPathData(); svg.remove(); return r.length === 2 && r[1].values[0] === 10; })()

assertions.description: getPathSegmentAtLength(15) on d="M0 0 L10 0 L10 10" returns the second line segment {type: "L", values: [10, 10]}, and returns null for an empty path.
assertions.test: (() => { const svg = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'svg'); const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); const e = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); if (typeof p.getPathSegmentAtLength !== 'function') return false; p.setAttribute('d', 'M0 0 L10 0 L10 10'); svg.append(p, e); document.body.append(svg); const r = p.getPathSegmentAtLength(15); const n = e.getPathSegmentAtLength(10); svg.remove(); return !!r && r.type === 'L' && r.values[0] === 10 && r.values[1] === 10 && n === null; })()
